# Composition report

Everything below is derived from the interfaces in `data/`. Nothing here is maintained by hand: no file records which use case enables which, which requirement has no supplier, or which two use cases overlap.

Regenerate with `python3 build/build.py`; `build/queries.py` answers the same questions interactively.

## Worked compositions

A chain is reported only if every step earns its place - drop any one of them and the goal is no longer reachable.

### Electronic identity to an open banking relationship, and its refresh

The chain the ecosystem is actually built on. Note that nothing in it names a credential: each step asks for a condition, and the e-ID happens to be what substantiates the first one.

**Electronic identity held** → `identity-verification` → `due-diligence-onboarding` → `due-diligence-refresh` → **KYC attestation current**

- `identity-verification` — needs Identity evidence available; provides Identity verified
- `due-diligence-onboarding` — needs Identity verified; provides Customer relationship open
- `due-diligence-refresh` — needs Customer relationship open, Due diligence evidence available; provides KYC attestation current

### Education qualification to university admission

Admission asks for a verified qualification, not for a Maturitätszeugnis, so any flow that can establish the qualification serves it.

**Upper-secondary qualification held** → `eid-issuance` → `identity-verification` → `qualification-verification` → `tertiary-admission` → **Tertiary enrolment established**

- `eid-issuance` — needs nothing; provides Electronic identity held
- `identity-verification` — needs Identity evidence available; provides Identity verified
- `qualification-verification` — needs Education qualification evidence available; provides Qualification verified
- `tertiary-admission` — needs Identity verified, Qualification verified; provides Tertiary enrolment established

### Education qualification to employment

The same two upstream patterns feed a different downstream one. Neither the issuance nor the verification pattern knows or cares which.

**Upper-secondary qualification held** → `eid-issuance` → `identity-verification` → `qualification-verification` → `employment-engagement` → **Employment relationship open**

- `eid-issuance` — needs nothing; provides Electronic identity held
- `identity-verification` — needs Identity evidence available; provides Identity verified
- `qualification-verification` — needs Education qualification evidence available; provides Qualification verified
- `employment-engagement` — needs Identity verified, Qualification verified; provides Employment relationship open

### Electronic identity to a proven age threshold

One step: age verification is not identity verification, and the interface says so - it consumes identity evidence and provides an attribute, never an identity.

**Electronic identity held** → `age-threshold-verification` → **Age attribute proven**

- `age-threshold-verification` — needs Identity evidence available; provides Age attribute proven

## Alternative evidence for one requirement

The test of whether conditions and credentials are really separate: can a second credential satisfy an existing requirement without any canonical use case changing?

**Due diligence evidence available** is required by `due-diligence-refresh`.

It can be substantiated by:

- **KYC attestation** — issued by `banking-kyc-onboarding-ch`
- **KYC currency attestation** — issued by `banking-re-kyc-ch`

No use case pattern names either credential, so a third one can be added to `data/credential-conditions.csv` and every use case requiring this condition accepts it immediately.

**Education qualification evidence available** is required by `qualification-verification`.

It can be substantiated by:

- **Upper-secondary school-leaving certificate** — issued by `education-matura-issuance-ch`
- **Vocational qualification certificate** — issued by `education-efz-issuance-ch`

No use case pattern names either credential, so a third one can be added to `data/credential-conditions.csv` and every use case requiring this condition accepts it immediately.

## Overlapping use case patterns

Candidates for editorial review, not decisions. Two patterns are reported when they share a primary function and their interfaces relate. Nothing is merged automatically: a shared shape may still be genuinely different work.

| Relation | Pattern | Pattern | Shared primary function |
|---|---|---|---|
| overlap | `credential-recovery-reidentification` | `legal-capacity-reidentification` | Identity lifecycle management |
| overlap | `due-diligence-onboarding` | `tertiary-admission` | Relationship onboarding |
| overlap | `eid-issuance` | `education-qualification-issuance` | Certification and attestation |

**`credential-recovery-reidentification` ~ `legal-capacity-reidentification`** (overlap)

- `credential-recovery-reidentification` needs Customer relationship open, Identity verified; provides Access granted
- `legal-capacity-reidentification` needs Customer relationship open, Identity verified; provides Legal capacity established

**`due-diligence-onboarding` ~ `tertiary-admission`** (overlap)

- `due-diligence-onboarding` needs Identity verified; provides Customer relationship open, KYC attestation held
- `tertiary-admission` needs Identity verified, Qualification verified; provides Tertiary enrolment established, Tertiary enrolment evidence held

**`eid-issuance` ~ `education-qualification-issuance`** (overlap)

- `eid-issuance` needs nothing; provides Electronic identity held
- `education-qualification-issuance` needs Identity verified; provides Upper-secondary qualification held

## Gaps

Where the classification and the ecosystem do not yet meet.

### Requirements with no upstream provider

- `accreditation-verification` requires **Accreditation evidence available** — no use case here provides it

### Principal outcomes with no downstream consumer

### Use case patterns with no implementation

None: every pattern has at least one flow.

### Value stream stages with no use case

19 of 26 stages. The graph covers a slice of each stream, and the stages below mark where a use case could be added without inventing a new classification.

**Hire to retire**

- Agree and sign the employment contract (`agree-and-sign`)
- Provision and later revoke access (`provision-access`)
- Retain the employment record (`retain-employment-record`)
**Order to cash**

- Agree and sign (`agree-and-sign`)
- Decide the terms to offer (`decide-terms`)
- Deliver (`deliver`)
- Handle what goes wrong (`handle-requests`)
- Invoice and collect (`invoice-and-collect`)
- Retain the audit trail (`retain-audit-trail`)
**Procure to pay**

- Agree and sign (`agree-and-sign`)
- Assess counterparty and financial risk (`assess-risk`)
- Check conformity of what will be supplied (`check-conformity`)
- Clear the border (`clear-border`)
- Establish provenance through delivery (`establish-provenance`)
- Establish the supplier is a real legal entity (`establish-supplier-identity`)
- Goods receipt against specification (`goods-receipt`)
- Invoice and payment (`invoice-and-pay`)
- Retain the audit trail (`retain-audit-trail`)
- Substantiate the tax position (`substantiate-tax`)
